prf:terminal-resolution:
Proof Proof of the pair Skein nucleon identities. Write D = q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}. Substituting \mathcal{S}_{ab} = (q\mu_a + q^{-1}\mu_b)/D from the pair Skein mass formula into the two nucleon sums gives

  D\,m_p = (3q + q^{-1})\,\mu_{\mathfrak{u}} + 2q^{-1}\,\mu_{\mathfrak{d}},
  \qquad
  D\,m_n = 2q\,\mu_{\mathfrak{u}} + (q + 3q^{-1})\,\mu_{\mathfrak{d}}.

Part (i). The cross term 2\mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}} appears in both sums and cancels in the difference, leaving

  m_n - m_p = \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}} - \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}}
  = \frac{(q + q^{-1})(\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}})}{D}.

Part (ii). The coefficient matrix of the linear form above has determinant

  (3q + q^{-1})(q + 3q^{-1}) - (2q^{-1})(2q) = 3q^2 + 6 + 3q^{-2} = 3\,[2]_q^2 .

Dividing by D^2 gives the determinant of the map. Under the hypotheses (3, D and [2]_q invertible), the determinant is invertible, and Cramer's rule gives the two-sided inverse

  \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} = \frac{D\bigl((q + 3q^{-1})\,m_p - 2q^{-1}\,m_n\bigr)}{3\,[2]_q^2},
  \qquad
  \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} = \frac{D\bigl((3q + q^{-1})\,m_n - 2q\,m_p\bigr)}{3\,[2]_q^2}.

Substituting these into the linear form returns (m_p, m_n), and substituting the linear form into these returns (\mu_{\mathfrak{u}}, \mu_{\mathfrak{d}}), so the map is a bijection. Both parts are identities in q; no value of q and no measured mass is used. \square

Remark Q-value predictions vs experiment: q-weighted channel separation. The q-weighted method evaluates \beta^- decay Q-values from q with zero fitted parameters. The figures in Table and the first two subsections below record an unregenerated float64 evaluation at the auxiliary loop parameter z_{\mathrm{aux}} = q^{1/2}/(q+1); they are not reproduced at the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), whose bare and combined evaluations are tabulated in the spectral-decomposition interpretation.

See Table.

At z_{\mathrm{aux}} = q^{1/2}/(q+1) the q-weighted table had MAE \approx 4.4\% and RMS \approx 5.4\% (errors \leq 2.2\% for A \leq 14), using hard-coded heavy-nucleus factors F_{\mathrm{deg2}} = 0.5904 and F_{\mathrm{Pauli}} = 0.6382. At the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), neither constant holds: the Rosso–Jones ratio evaluates to F_{\mathrm{deg2}} \approx 3.68442 > 1 (an amplification rather than a suppression), and the Markov-trace Pauli factor vanishes identically because y_{(1^3)} = 0 at z = q^3/(q^2+1).

Worked example: {}^{90}\mathrm{Sr}.

At z_{\mathrm{aux}} = q^{1/2}/(q+1), the bare q-weighted figure \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{bare}} \approx 0.944\,\mathrm{MeV} exceeded \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{exp}} = 0.546\,\mathrm{MeV} by +73\%, and multiplying by 0.5904 gave Q \approx 0.557\,\mathrm{MeV} (+2.1\%). At z = q^3/(q^2+1), using the corollary normalisation |\log_q(P_{\mathrm{dau}}/P_{\mathrm{par}})|\cdot\hbar_q\cdot m_e/3, the bare term is \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{bare}} \approx 0.05482\,\mathrm{MeV} (-90.0\%) and the combined formula gives Q \approx 0.20198\,\mathrm{MeV} (-63.0\%).

Evaluation at z = q^3/(q^2+1).

At z = q^3/(q^2+1), recomputing the corollary's bare term and combined formula across six benchmark decays yields residuals of 8–98\% (bare) and 1–100\% (combined); the q-weighted unbinding/rebinding stage and a non-vanishing replacement for the filled-shell Pauli projection have not yet been derived at z = q^3/(q^2+1).

Method.

The method uses the eigenvalue asymmetry q versus -q^{-1} of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra to separate unbinding, rebinding and spectator channels. The shell correction factors were intended to derive from the 6 \times 6 regular representation of H_3(q).

Error structure.

The parametric uncertainty \delta Q / \delta q_0 is negligible. The residual errors stem from the shell correction and, at z = q^3/(q^2+1), from the vanishing of the (1^3) Pauli branch. Improving F_{\mathrm{shell}} requires extending the spectral decomposition (spectral decomposition).

Ground-state character of \mathcal{N}(7,7). For p = n = 7, every crossing is a \mathfrak{p}-\mathfrak{n} mixed crossing. No crossing incurs the Coulomb penalty (q - q^{-1})/2 \approx 0.105, and none carries the attractive excess -(q - q^{-1})/2.

This constitutes the maximal braid shortcut: all 26 crossings contribute identically. The alternation prevents any generator from appearing twice consecutively, so the Hecke reduction encounters no \sigma_i^2 terms. This renders the Gröbner--Shirshov normal form maximally efficient.

Instability of \mathcal{N}(6,8). For p = 6 and n = 8, the 8 neutrons generate 4 \mathfrak{n}-\mathfrak{n} crossings (e.g., between neutrons 7–8, 7–9) that break alternation. These same-species crossings carry weight q^{-1} rather than (q + q^{-1})/2, introducing three penalties:

rem:trace-ratio-interpretation:
Remark Trace ratio computational results and the half-life formula. Computational results. The trace ratio \hat{V}^{\mathrm{par}} / \hat{V}^{\mathrm{dau}} at each affected generator is tabulated for all six verification nuclei in Table: Trace ratio per affected generator.

The trace ratio grows with p (the number of affected generators), reflecting the increasing number of crossings that change type. The squared ratio |\mathcal{M}_q|^2 spans 10 orders of magnitude. The observed variation in nuclear matrix elements is smaller: \log ft from 3 to 9 corresponds to |M|^2 spanning \sim 10^6. The two are the same kind of quantity and the model range brackets the observed one, but it over-spans it by about four orders of magnitude, so this is a consistency-of-scale remark and not a quantitative match.

The growth of the ratio with p means heavier nuclei have larger topological matrix elements, which drives faster decay rates. This aligns with the observation that allowed beta transitions in heavy nuclei tend to have shorter half-lives (smaller \log ft) than those in light nuclei.

The half-life formula (final form). Combine the trace ratio with the phase space integral:

  t_{1/2}
  = 
  \frac{\ln 2 \cdot 2N_v^4}{243\mathfrak{E}_{\times} \cdot \mu_0}
   \cdot 
  \frac{1}{[2]_q  \cdot  s^2}
   \cdot 
  \frac{1}{f(Z_d, Q)}
   \cdot 
  \prod_{i=0}^{p}
  \left|
    \frac{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{dau}}}{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{par}}}
  \right|^2

Here s = q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2} is the Skein amplitude, \mathfrak{E}_{\times} = \frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) is the crossing energy, \mu_0 is the single dimensional scale, and N_v is the effective crossing count of the weak scale (v = N_v\mathfrak{E}_{\times}\mu_0). By Categorical neutrality of saturated shells: full-twist identity action on \Phi_n at magic n, the categorical mass at level Z is supported on a single self-conjugate partition \lambda_Z \vdash Z, and \Phi_N is similarly supported on \mu_N \vdash N with \mu_N = \mu_N'. The LR-fusion at level A = Z + N is rigid:

for a uniquely determined self-conjugate u_{ZN} \vdash A with u_{ZN} = u_{ZN}' and c( u_{ZN}) = 0. The LR multiplicity is one (c^{ u_{ZN}}_{\lambda_Z, \mu_N} = 1), and all other LR coefficients vanish. Equivalently, \sum_{x \in u_{ZN}} c(x) = 0: the categorical mass at the double-magic level A is supported strictly on the single self-conjugate Specht module V_{ u_{ZN}}, with no off-diagonal Wedderburn capacity to absorb crossing energy beyond the Coulomb, Casimir, and pairing terms already present at \lambda_Z and \mu_N.

Remark (the rigidity fails for genuine LR coefficients). With c^{ u}_{\lambda\mu} the Littlewood–Richardson coefficient, counted as LR tableaux of shape u/\lambda and content \mu, the statement above cannot hold for any Z, N \in \mathfrak{M}. For nonempty \lambda, \mu the row sum \lambda + \mu (row lengths added) always occurs, c^{\lambda+\mu}_{\lambda\mu} \geq 1: fill row i of (\lambda+\mu)/\lambda with the value i. Rigidity therefore forces u_{ZN} = \lambda_Z + \mu_N. The first row of \lambda + \mu has \lambda_1 + \mu_1 cells, while its first column has \max(\lambda_1, \mu_1) cells when \lambda = \lambda' and \mu = \mu', so \lambda + \mu is not self-conjugate. Self-conjugacy of u_{ZN} follows from rigidity and the conjugation symmetry c^{ u'}_{\lambda'\mu'} = c^{ u}_{\lambda\mu}, so the two requirements are incompatible.
rem:diagrammatic-double-magic-lr-fusion-:
Remark LR-fusion rigidity: setup, mechanism, examples, and predictions. This remark records the setup, mechanism, worked cases, higher-magic predictions, and proof outlook for Conjecture (diagrammatic double-magic): LR-fusion rigidity at Z, N \in \mathfrak{M}.

A nuclide is double-magic when its proton and neutron counts both fall in \mathfrak{M} = \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\}. Canonical examples include ^4\mathrm{He}, ^{16}\mathrm{O}, ^{40}\mathrm{Ca}, ^{48}\mathrm{Ca}, ^{56}\mathrm{Ni}, ^{132}\mathrm{Sn}, and ^{208}\mathrm{Pb}. The empirical signature is exceptional binding-energy stability: these nuclei occupy sharp local maxima on the binding-per-nucleon curve. The Littlewood-Richardson (LR) fusion of the two saturated Z- and N-blocks is rigid (a single self-conjugate Specht module on the diagonal) and permits no off-diagonal flux.

conj:double-magic-delta-i-bound:
Conjecture Empirical double-magic isotopes satisfy |\Delta i| \leq 1 across Bring shell indices. Let (i_Z, i_N) \in \{1, \ldots, 7\} \times \{1, \ldots, 7\} be the Bring shell indices of an isotope's proton and neutron magic numbers. Define \Delta i := i_N - i_Z. Then every empirically observed doubly-magic isotope has

  \Delta i \;\in\; \{0, 1\}.

No isotope with \Delta i \geq 2 is doubly-magic.
sec:beta-decay-magic-shells-k12-barrier-:
Direct matrix diagonalisation of the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_A(q) grows factorially with mass number A, encountering a computational wall around strand count k = 12. By exploiting the two-row Temperley–Lieb quotient at z = q^3/(q^2+1) and the homological residue of the graded trace, the categorical pipeline bypasses the k = 12 matrix barrier analytically.

This section proves the double-magic \Delta I bound, establishes the k = 12 homological barrier-bypass theorem, derives the nuclear magic numbers \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} from the per-partition character zeros at q_0 and the S_5-equivariant Bring period lattice, and maps the graded-trace residue onto the Bethe–Weizsäcker mass decomposition and Strutinsky's shell correction.
